reasons.experiments: Both papers cover four or five datasets, four model classes, two estimators, budget sweeps and other variation sources as yardsticks; Paper A adds a test of shap defaults with a resampled background and a single-run certificate tied to explicit pre-stated claims C1-C5 (pages 3-5), and Paper B adds l1_reg and log-odds checks and a compute-matched repeat-versus-enlarge analysis, so the two are comparably rich.
reasons.page_use: Paper A's body ends early on page 7 of an 8-page ICML limit, which is somewhat thin, whereas Paper B fills the 9-page ICLR body well (pages 1-9).
reasons.clean_text: Both papers leak file names: Paper A mentions code/check_singular.py, results/tables/ and 'tabD' (pages 4, 8, 9); Paper B is worse, with REPRODUCE.md and 'world's meter' in the body (page 4), paper/make_numbers.py and 'the report role' (page 9), plan/*.md commit logs (page 17), and an AI-agent pipeline description (pages 9-10).
reasons.abstract_intro: Paper A's abstract and introduction (page 1) are crisp, state a falsifiable question, and lead into clearly numbered claims; Paper B's abstract (page 1) is long and dense with numbers, and its contributions list reads more like a delivery report.

reasons.title: Paper B's title (page 1) is somewhat tighter and more specific than Paper A's long three-line title (page 1), though both are question-style and acceptable.
reasons.figure1: Neither paper opens with an overview diagram; Paper A's Figure 1 (page 5) is a clean, well-labelled error and top-3 match grid, while Paper B's Figure 1 (page 4) is cramped, with tiny axis text and many overlapping coloured lines.
reasons.figures_tables: Paper A's figures and tables (pages 5–8, 16–20) share a consistent, readable style; Paper B's tables are clean, but Figures 2–3 (pages 5–6) are small with hard-to-read rotated labels.
reasons.experiments: Paper A gives a fuller grid (20 cells, 30 runs, exact references, retrain and background standards, a matched-compute repeat-vs-enlarge analysis, l1_reg and log-odds checks, retrain-fraction sensitivity on page 19); Paper B covers similar questions plus a single-run certificate (page 5), but with fewer runs and thinner per-cell support in the body.
reasons.page_use: Paper A fills the 9-page ICLR body (pages 1–9) with a substantive appendix, while Paper B's body ends partway through page 6 of an 8-page ICML limit, so its body is thin.
reasons.clean_text: Paper A has more pipeline talk (REPRODUCE.md and 'the world's meter' on page 4, script paths and the 'report role' remark on page 9, plan/CHANGES.md and empty appendix headings on page 17); Paper B is cleaner but still has a stray 'tabD' on page 4 and code/results paths on page 9.
reasons.abstract_intro: Paper B has a concise abstract and an introduction with an explicit claims list (pages 1–3); Paper A's abstract (page 1) is dense with numbers but its introduction and related work (pages 1–2) are well argued and flow like a conference paper.

reasons.title: Paper A's title (p1) is concise and specific, while Paper B's two-line title with subtitle (p1) is long, so A is better on this point.
reasons.figure1: Neither paper opens with an overview diagram: Paper A's Figure 1 (p6) is a 3x3 grid of adequacy-vs-work plots with a very long caption, and Paper B's Figure 1 (p5) is a dense but informative error/top-3 match grid across 5 datasets; the two are roughly comparable.
reasons.figures_tables: Paper B's figures and tables (pp5-8, 11-20) are consistent and readable, though a few appendix subsection headers are empty (A.1, A.2, B on pp11, 17). Paper A's figures are clean, but their captions are extremely long and repetitive (pp21-41), and several appendix pages hold only a small table.
reasons.experiments: Paper B covers 5 datasets x 4 models and compares single-run noise against retraining, background redraws and chance (p7). It also tests repeat versus enlarge at matched compute (p8), margin-based conditions (p6), and library defaults/log-odds (p7), which is richer support for the central claim than Paper A's 3x3 grid with one background-sensitivity arm (pp5-7).
reasons.page_use: Both bodies fill about 9 pages before references on p10. Paper B cites about 17 references against Paper A's 12, and Paper A pads its total to 48 pages with a checklist and repetitive appendix figures.
reasons.clean_text: Paper A puts a config path in the body (analysis/configs/main.json, p3) and fills its appendix with shell commands and script paths (pp13-15, 18-19). Paper B mostly limits file names to the reproducibility statement, but REPRODUCE.md appears in the body (p4).
reasons.abstract_intro: Paper B's abstract and introduction (p1-2) state the question, contributions and negative results clearly in NeurIPS/ICLR style. Paper A's abstract and introduction (p1-2) are heavily hedged and jargon-dense ('declared adequacy event', 'conservative boundary interval'), which makes them hard to follow.

reasons.title: Paper A's title (p1) is informative but long and two-part; Paper B's 'Single-run SHAP reliability under finite computation' (p1) is concise and specific, so B is slightly better here.
reasons.figure1: Paper A's Figure 1 (p5) is a dense, informative grid of error and top-3 match against budget for every cell; Paper B's Figure 1 (p6) is a 3x3 grid of adequacy curves pinned near 1.0 that conveys little; neither is an overview diagram, but A's is more informative.
reasons.figures_tables: Paper A has consistent figures (Figs 1-4, pp5-8) with readable captions and clean tables (Table 1, p5); Paper B's main-text figures are few, and its appendix figures carry very long repetitive captions and tables floating on mostly empty pages (pp12, 20, 23-26).
reasons.experiments: Paper A covers 5 datasets and 4 models with Kernel and permutation SHAP, comparison standards (retraining, background, null), repeat-versus-enlarge at matched compute, l1_reg and log-odds checks, and a margin analysis (pp4-8); Paper B covers 3 datasets and 3 models with mostly saturated results (adequacy near 1) and fewer comparisons.
reasons.page_use: Paper A's body fills about 9 pages with limitations before the statements (pp1-9); Paper B's body ends early on p9 with half the page empty, and both have short reference lists.
reasons.clean_text: Paper A mentions REPRODUCE.md and paper/numbers.tex in the body (pp4, 9) and plan file paths in the appendix (p17); Paper B puts analysis/configs/main.json in the main text (p3) and many script paths and shell commands in the appendix (pp13-15, 18-19), so B is worse.
reasons.abstract_intro: Paper A's abstract (p1) is number-heavy but states clear findings, and its intro and related work (pp1-2) are well argued; Paper B's abstract and intro (p1) are hedged and stilted, with phrasing like 'interrupted elapsed clocks are retained'.
